title: Drop the rough sleeping programme
name: Drop the rough sleeping programme
headline: Drop rough sleeping programme. Saves £0.1bn in 2029-30.
description: The Budget funds a route off the streets for rough sleepers in England to 2028-29, with longer-term accommodation and support, partly from existing housing budgets. Switch this on to drop it.

baselinePolicy.text: A route off the streets is funded from autumn 2026 to 2028-29, partly by reprioritising existing MHCLG budgets (Table 6.1 lines 33 and 34).

source.quote: This measure will provide an offer of a route off the streets to rough sleepers in England from Autumn 2026 until 2028-29, alongside longer-term accommodation and intensive support.

alreadyIncludes: A route off the streets is funded from autumn 2026 to 2028-29, partly by reprioritising existing MHCLG budgets (Table 6.1 lines 33 and 34).

lines.title: Rough Sleeping: Invest in a route off the streets across the Parliament, alongside longer-term accommodation and intensive support
Rough Sleeping: Reprioritise existing MHCLG budgets to tackle rough sleeping

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury’s costing with the sign kept (a line that reduced borrowing is spending the reversal adds back; a line that cost money is spending the reversal saves).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
The two lines net: the new money less what MHCLG moves from its own budgets in 2026-27 and 2027-28.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
